claims_and_derivations.claim: In the strong-coupling adiabatic limit for an axially symmetric nucleus, collective rotation about the symmetry axis represents a continuous gauge symmetry (collective rotational degree of freedom is absent, J_parallel = 0), and the projection K on the symmetry axis is carried by intrinsic quasiparticle alignment j_intr,3 = K. The collective rotational energy is E_K(I) - E_intr = hbar^2 [I(I+1) - K^2] / (2 J_perp) for I >= K. Bandhead spin I_bandhead = K holds in this model under allowed signature/parity conditions; observed bandhead can differ in real nuclei.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Shimizu 2005 preprint PDF p. 3 Eq.(9); BM-II p. 190; manuscript Eq.(3-4-high-K-spectrum)
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Adiabatic strong-coupling, K > 1/2 Coriolis decoupling neglected; intrinsic state fixed; not universal to non-adiabatic or triaxial systems.

claims_and_derivations.claim: The laboratory adjacent-spin transition energy in a fixed-K band is Delta E_lab(I -> I-1) = hbar^2 I / J_perp, with the first transition above bandhead Delta E_lab(K+1 -> K) = hbar^2 (K+1) / J_perp, approaching hbar^2 K / J_perp as K >> 1.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Shimizu 2005 preprint PDF p. 3 Eqs.(10)-(11); manuscript Eqs.(3-4-lab-spacing)-(3-4-asymptotic-lab-spacing)
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Fixed intrinsic K; delta I = 1 laboratory transitions; ideal constant moment of inertia.

claims_and_derivations.claim: The small-amplitude wobbling frequency omega_wob in the co-rotating intrinsic frame at fixed spin I is conceptually and operationally distinct from the cross-spin energy spacing Delta E_lab in the laboratory frame. In the axially symmetric limit of the adiabatic RPA (Shimizu et al. 2005), the two are rigorously connected by omega_wob = omega_prec - omega_rot, where omega_prec = hbar K / J_perp^(eff) is the lab precession frequency and omega_rot = hbar I / J_x is the frame cranking frequency.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Shimizu 2005 preprint PDF pp. 2-3 Eqs.(5)-(8); PDF pp. 5-6 Sec. III B Eqs.(32)-(39); manuscript Eq.(3-4-shimizu-connection)
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Axially symmetric limit about rotation axis (J_y = J_z = J_perp) in adiabatic RPA; does not imply generic triaxial TW is isomorphic to high-K precession, nor that they are disconnected.

claims_and_derivations.claim: In the tilted precession (TiP) model (Lawrie et al. 2020), 3D rotation in odd-A triaxial nuclei arises from orientation competition between valence quasiparticle alignment along a preferred geometric principal axis and core rotation about the maximum-inertia axis. This tilts the stationary rotation axis into a principal plane (e.g. s-m plane). Total angular momentum precesses about this tilted direction; bands with larger tilt angles are TiP bands.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Lawrie 2020 PRC 101, 034306 pp. 2-3 Eqs.(1)-(6), Figs.1-3; p. 5 Sec. III, Eqs.(19)-(22); manuscript Sec. 3.4.2
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Particle-rotor coupling framework with frozen j in comparison; model mechanism, not directly observable classical time trajectory; no universal gamma or spin boundaries.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Harmonic wobbling is an extreme small-amplitude approximation to 3D rotation / TiP, valid only when the transverse angular momentum components satisfy f(n, I) << 1 and the excitation energies and transition probabilities scale linearly with phonon number n. For typical transverse coupling parameters in 135Pr and 105Pd, f remains large (f1 > 0.45), meaning the strict harmonic wobbling approximation does not automatically hold.
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Calculated within QTR model with stated parameters and frozen j; energy decrease Delta E(I) is not a unique or universal criterion for TiP or wobbling.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Finite-I quantum wave functions in orientation space are discrete quantum states, generally not continuous Gaussians. An exact center nodal line with strictly zero density and symmetric double peaks for n=1 holds only in an idealized 1D symmetric harmonic oscillator; realistic nuclear Hamiltonians with asymmetric curvatures, Coriolis coupling, and parity/signature mixing break this reflection symmetry. Angular spread Delta theta ~ 1/sqrt(I) requires stable quadratic curvature and low n << I far from soft modes and separatrices.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Lawrie 2020 p. 3 Figs.2-3; BM-II Chapter 4; manuscript Sec. 3.4.3
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Finite-spin quantum mechanics; theoretical probability density is not directly measurable in real-time experiments; physical testing proceeds via observable energies and EM transitions.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Small-amplitude wobbling phonon tagging requires localization in the quadratic expansion basin where higher-order terms are small. It does not require all three inertias to be distinct (high-K axisymmetric limit has local expansion), nor that j never reorients. Competing mechanisms for companion bands with smoothly varying Delta E(I) include: signature partner bands (alpha = +- 1/2), quasiparticle configuration crossings, and dynamic coupling to a gamma-soft core.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Petrache 2006 PRL 96, 112502; Lv 2022 PLB 827, 136840; Nomura 2022 PRC 105, 024320; manuscript Sec. 3.4.4
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Transitional A approx 130 nuclei with shallow triaxial minima; competing interpretations require case-by-case data analysis.

claims_and_derivations.claim: Multi-dimensional spectroscopic criteria: (1) DCO ratio R_DCO(delta) is a quadratic rational function of multipole mixing ratio delta(E2/M1); solving it yields two real roots, a degenerate root, or no real root. Measuring linear polarization P aids in parity distinction but does not guarantee unique disambiguation under all experimental uncertainties. (2) delta(E2/M1) is rigorously defined as radiation emission amplitude ratio with full operator units (mu_N, e fm^2, and E_gamma/(hbar c)). (3) Interband B(E2) ~ 1/I and strong M1 suppression are asymptotic limits of idealized harmonic models, not universal laws. (4) Scientific confirmation relies on forward joint prediction of self-consistent models against multi-observable networks and critical falsification of competing hypotheses.
claims_and_derivations.locator: Lange et al. 1982 RMP 54, 119; Frauendorf 2014 PRC 89, 014322; manuscript Sec. 3.4.5
claims_and_derivations.conditions: Oriented nuclear radiation theory; experimental detector geometry and efficiency calibration; realistic nuclei deviate from idealized 1/I.
